persecution_claim: Applicant is a commercial maize farmer in the Free State province. On 14 March 2021, a group of five armed men forced entry to his farmhouse, assaulted him and his wife, and stole cash and livestock. Police response was delayed and dismissive. Since then, the applicant has received repeated threats via SMS demanding he abandon his land, referencing 'expropriation without compensation.' In September 2022, his neighbor, also a farmer, was killed in a similar attack. Applicant fled to Johannesburg after local officials declined to investigate the threats, stating land must be returned to the 'rightful owners.' His farm has been listed for potential expropriation under local policy.
education_occupation: Bachelor's degree in Agriculture; commercial farmer

persecution_claim: Applicant owns a small hardware business in a rural town in Western Cape. On 25 January 2022, her shop was firebombed at night, causing extensive damage. CCTV footage showed masked individuals, and a note was left stating 'Boer, leave before you are removed.' She reported the incident, but police wrote a case number and took no further action, suggesting it was a 'land dispute' or 'local politics.' She subsequently received a phone call warning her that she would be killed if she reopened the store. She moved to Cape Town but was found and threatened again. She fears for her life due to her ethnicity and perceived economic privilege.
education_occupation: High school diploma; small business owner

persecution_claim: Applicant, a schoolteacher, lived in a village near Kharkiv. In April 2022, during an occupation by Russian forces, soldiers set up a checkpoint in front of her home. They repeatedly harassed her, demanding that she teach a pro-Russian curriculum and inform on local residents. On April 17, 2022, she was detained for two days and beaten when she refused to cooperate. One soldier threatened her with a weapon and stated, 'You will cooperate or disappear.' After the Ukrainian army retook the area, she fled with her children to western Ukraine. She remains terrified of further occupation and has documented injuries consistent with her account.
education_occupation: Master's degree in Education; teacher

persecution_claim: Applicant, a retired engineer, resided in Mariupol. During the siege in March 2022, his apartment building was shelled and destroyed. He was forced to shelter in a basement for three weeks without food, water, or medicine for his heart condition. When he and his neighbors emerged, they were stopped by Russian soldiers who accused him of being a 'Jewish nationalist' and confiscated his documents. He was held briefly and then released, but his home and all possessions were gone. He fled to Kyiv and then to Poland via a humanitarian corridor. He fears being targeted again due to his Jewish identity and nationality.
education_occupation: Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering; retired

persecution_claim: Applicant, a software engineer from Moscow, openly opposed the invasion of Ukraine. On March 5, 2022, he attended a solo protest near the Kremlin holding a sign saying 'Stop the War.' He was immediately arrested, taken to a police station, and held for 12 hours. He was charged under Article 20.3.3 of the Russian Criminal Code (discrediting the armed forces) and fined. Shortly thereafter, he was fired from his job due to pressure on his employer. He received online threats and was briefly detained again after a neighbor reported him for his anti-war posts on social media. Fearing imprisonment and continued harassment, he fled to Georgia.
education_occupation: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science; software engineer

persecution_claim: Applicant, a lawyer in Minsk, served as a legal observer during the 2020 presidential election protests. On August 10, 2020, she was detained by riot police while documenting arrests outside a polling station. She was beaten, her phone was confiscated, and she was charged with 'participating in an unsanctioned rally.' She was sentenced to 15 days in detention. After release, she was followed and her apartment was searched without a warrant. She was eventually dismissed from her legal position due to official pressure. Fearing further arrests and a longer prison sentence, she fled to Lithuania with her teenage daughter.
education_occupation: Master's degree in Law; lawyer (previously employed)

rsc: RSC Middle East and North Africa
persecution_claim: Applicant, a businessman in Shiraz, is a practicing Baha'i. In 2021, the Revolutionary Guard seized his carpet shop without legal justification, claiming it was a 'front for anti-government activity.' He was arrested for three days and questioned about his religious beliefs. Upon release, he was informed his business license was revoked. His oldest daughter was dismissed from a university in 2022 after her Baha'i identity was discovered, and she was barred from attending any further university. The family has faced systematic social and economic exclusion. He has received threats warning him to leave the country or face further consequences.
education_occupation: High school diploma; small business owner (former)

rsc: RSC Middle East and North Africa
persecution_claim: Applicant, a graphic designer, converted from Islam to Christianity in 2021 and began attending an underground house church in Tehran. In July 2022, a raid was conducted on the meeting location. Several attendees were arrested, but she managed to escape through a window. Her home was raided the following day, and her computer and bible were seized. The Ministry of Intelligence has issued a summons for her, accusing her of 'waging war against God.' Two of her fellow church members have received lengthy prison sentences. She went into hiding, moving between safe houses, before illegally crossing the border into Turkey.
education_occupation: Bachelor's degree in Graphic Design; freelance designer

persecution_claim: Applicant served as a translator for the US military from 2008 to 2014. He was granted a Special Immigrant Visa (SIV) but was unable to depart before the Taliban takeover in August 2021. On August 20, 2021, the Taliban came to his home in Kabul, searched it for papers, and beat his brother who attempted to protect them. They left a 'night letter' ordering the applicant to report to the Taliban court for 'collaborating with the crusaders.' His brother was shot and killed by Taliban fighters a week later at a checkpoint, an act the applicant believes was intentional. He fled to Pakistan with his wife and daughter.
education_occupation: Bachelor's degree in Economics; former interpreter

persecution_claim: Applicant, a former teacher in Bamyan, was fired from her position in September 2021 shortly after the Taliban return, with a directive that women are not allowed to work. She then began receiving threats from Taliban members for her previous work as a teacher with girls, which they called 'haram.' In November 2022, her family attempted to force her to marry a Taliban commander as their 'protector.' She refused and escaped the family home, fearing for her life. She traveled to Kabul and then to Pakistan alone. She has no support network and fears being located and forcibly returned.
education_occupation: Bachelor's degree in Education; former teacher

persecution_claim: The applicant, a Pentecostal Christian, was arrested at her home in Asmara on 14 August 2022 by National Security agents. She was detained at Mai Serwa prison for 9 months. During detention, she was subjected to sleep deprivation and forced to sign a renunciation of her faith. She refused and was beaten. She was released in May 2023 but immediately received call-up papers for indefinite national service. She fled after her church pastor was arrested for holding an unauthorized service in June 2023. She fears return due to her religious affiliation and refusal to serve indefinitely.
education_occupation: Secondary school; former market trader

persecution_claim: The applicant fled Eritrea in 2021 after being conscripted into the national service for a third time. He had already served two terms and was called up again in July 2021. He refused to report and went into hiding. In September 2021, military police raided his village in Keren, searching for him and beating his elderly mother. He fled to Ethiopia. He claims he would be subjected to indefinite service and potential detention if returned. He also attends an underground Pentecostal fellowship in Addis Ababa.
education_occupation: High school graduate; former mechanic apprentice

persecution_claim: The applicant and her family fled their home in Gondar in March 2021 following attacks by Fano militiamen and subsequent government airstrikes against the militia in civilian areas. Her husband was killed when a mortar struck their neighborhood in April 2021. She fled with her four children to Sudan in May 2021. She fears returning to Ethiopia due to ongoing conflict in the Amhara region, arbitrary detention of Amhara men, and the risk of violence from all sides. She is the sole provider for her family.
education_occupation: Primary education; farmer (coffee cultivation)

persecution_claim: The applicant, a member of the Bantu minority group, fled Somalia in 2018 after Al-Shabaab attempted to forcibly recruit his 16-year-old son. They threatened to kill the family if the son did not join. The son was taken in June 2018, but escaped three days later. The family fled to Kenya. While in Kenya, the applicant received reports that Al-Shabaab had killed his uncle in 2022, seeking to establish their control over the family. He fears that returning to Somalia would result in the forced recruitment of his son and retaliation against the family.
education_occupation: None; farmer

persecution_claim: The applicant fled El Geneina in June 2023 after a massacre of Masalit civilians by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and allied Arab militias. Her husband was killed in front of her, and her home was burned. She escaped to Chad with her young daughter. She was present during the 4 June 2023 attack where RSF fighters went door-to-door, killing men and older boys. She survived by hiding under a bed for three hours. She fears return to Darfur due to the ongoing ethnic cleansing against Masalit.
education_occupation: Primary education; housewife

persecution_claim: The applicant, a woman from North Kivu, was abducted by M23 rebels in March 2023 near Kitchanga. She was held for two weeks and repeatedly sexually assaulted. She escaped when the rebel camp was attacked by another armed group. She fled to Goma and then to Rwanda. She is pregnant as a result of the rape. She fears that if returned to DRC, she will be targeted by M23 for having escaped, and potentially killed. She also lacks support as her family was displaced.
education_occupation: Secondary school; former food vendor

persecution_claim: The applicant was abducted by suspected Boko Haram/ISWAP fighters from her village in Borno State in 2019 at age 19. They kidnapped her along with other girls to serve as cooks and forced companions. After 18 months, she managed to escape during a military operation. She was held in Sambisa Forest. Since her escape, she has faced and fears ongoing threats from the insurgent group who view her as a traitor. She also faces stigma and rejection from her community who believes she was 'corrupted' by the militants.
education_occupation: Some secondary school; no formal occupation

persecution_claim: The applicant, an Anglophone separatist supporter from Northwest Region, was arrested by Cameroonian gendarmerie in Bamenda in October 2022. He was detained for 12 days in a military camp where he was beaten and tortured for suspected affiliation with the Ambazonia fighters. He was only released after a bribe was paid by his family. Following his release, the gendarmerie continued to regularly monitor his home. He fled with his wife to Nigeria in January 2023 after receiving threats that he would be 'disappeared' if he remained.
education_occupation: University degree; former primary school teacher

rsc: RSC Middle East and North Africa
persecution_claim: The applicant, a Coptic Christian, owned a shop in Minya. In May 2023, a mob set fire to his shop following a false blasphemy accusation made by a neighbor. He was accused of insulting Islam after his business dispute over a repair contract escalated. The mob burned his store and beat him. Police arrested him for 'offending religious sensibilities', but he was released after a week without charge due to pressure. He and his wife fear further mob attacks and legal harassment if they remain.
education_occupation: Secondary school; small business owner (grocery)

persecution_claim: The applicant, a Haratine (descendant of slaves), was an activist with IRA-Mauritanie. In 2021, he was arrested and beaten by police while organizing a demonstration against the persistence of slavery in his village. He was detained for 10 days without a lawyer. He continued his activism, and in 2023, his landlord, a prominent Arab-Berber, evicted his family from their home as a form of intimidation for not performing 'traditional duties'. He was also threatened with being re-enslaved by his former master's family.
education_occupation: Primary education; day laborer

persecution_claim: The applicant, a Chin Baptist pastor, led a congregation of 120 in Falam township. In March 2021, Burma Army troops entered his church during Sunday service, accused him of harboring pro-democracy activists, and beat him with rifle butts. His church was burned in April 2021. He received a summons for arrest under Section 505(a) of the Penal Code in June 2021. He fled to Malaysia in August 2021. His wife and two children remain in hiding in Mizoram, India. The applicant's brother was arrested in February 2022 for attending a prayer meeting and remains detained in Tamu prison.
education_occupation: Theology degree, pastor

persecution_claim: The applicant and her family fled from Buthidaung, Rakhine State in August 2017 after the Myanmar military burned her village and shot her father dead in front of her. She has been living in Kutupalong refugee camp, Bangladesh since September 2017. Her husband was abducted by Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army members in December 2022 when he refused to pay extortion; his body was found two weeks later. She is a widow with five children. The Bangladesh police refuse to investigate. She cannot return to Myanmar due to the Citizenship Law that strips Rohingya of legal status.
education_occupation: Unemployed, former homemaker

persecution_claim: The applicant was a food vendor in Kashgar, Xinjiang. In October 2020, he was detained and sent to a vocational training center in Hotan for three months because his wife wore a hijab in public. After release, he was forced to attend re-education sessions weekly. In January 2022, he was detained again when police found a Quran hidden in his home. He was beaten and held for 45 days. He escaped to Pakistan via the Karakoram Highway in June 2022. His wife and two children remain in Xinjiang under constant surveillance. His brother-in-law was sentenced to 8 years for 'inciting separatism' in 2021.
education_occupation: High school graduate, food vendor

persecution_claim: The applicant attended an unregistered house church in Shenzhen's Nanshan District from 2019. In June 2022, the church was raided during a service; police arrested 14 attendees and accused them of 'illegal religious assembly.' She was charged with 'picking quarrels and provoking trouble' under Article 293 of the Chinese Criminal Code and detained for 17 days. Police confiscated her laptop, which contained biblical study materials. After release, she was forced to sign a statement renouncing Christianity. She continued practicing in secret and was reported by a neighbor in March 2023. She fled to Thailand on a tourist visa in April 2023.
education_occupation: Bachelor's degree in marketing, former office manager

persecution_claim: The applicant was born in Chongjin and defected to China in 2018 at age 16. He worked illegally as a construction laborer in Yanbian for three years. In July 2021, Chinese police detained him during a sweep for North Korean defectors and threatened to repatriate him. He fled to Laos in September 2021, then to Thailand, and eventually reached Kenya in March 2022 via a people-smuggling network. He fears return because North Korea imposes the death penalty for defectors under Article 58 of the Criminal Code. His parents remain in Chongjin; they have not been heard from since 2019.
education_occupation: Middle school education, construction laborer

persecution_claim: The applicant is an Ê-Đê Montagnard from Dak Lak province. In January 2021, local authorities demolished his house church, built on his own land, citing lack of a permit. He filed a complaint and was arrested for 'abusing democratic freedoms to infringe upon state interests' (Article 331 of the Penal Code) in March 2021. He was detained for 60 days in Buon Ma Thuot prison. After release, police confiscated his land-use certificate, and he cannot farm. His son was beaten by police in September 2022 for attending a clandestine worship service. The family cannot practice their religion openly and face constant harassment.
education_occupation: Primary education, subsistence farmer

persecution_claim: The applicant is an Ahmadi Muslim from Rabwah, Punjab. In October 2022, a local Sunni cleric filed a First Information Report (FIR) against him under Section 295-C of the Pakistan Penal Code (blasphemy), alleging he used Islamic terms in his Ahmadi prayer call. Police arrested him and he spent 45 days in jail before being released on bail. His local mosque was sealed by the district administration in November 2022. He received multiple death threats from Tehreek-e-Labbaik activists. He cannot work as a pharmacist because his Ahmadi identity is disclosed on his CNIC. His children have been expelled from school.
education_occupation: Pharmacy degree, registered pharmacist

persecution_claim: The applicant worked as a bonded laborer in a brick kiln in Kasur, Punjab, for 12 years until 2020, indebted to the kiln owner for a loan of 50,000 PKR that he could never repay. When he attempted to leave, the owner beat him with a shovel in April 2021, breaking his right arm. In August 2022, a landlord attempted to forcibly convert his 14-year-old daughter to Islam, threatening to file a blasphemy case against the family if they refused. Police refused to register a complaint. The family fled to Lahore in October 2022 and live in hiding in a church shelter. The kiln owner has threatened to kill the applicant if he returns.
education_occupation: Illiterate, brick kiln laborer

rsc: RSC Middle East and North Africa
persecution_claim: The applicant was captured by ISIS in Sinjar in August 2014. She was held as a sex slave for three years in Mosul and Raqqa, sold among multiple fighters. She was forced to convert to Islam and bear a child from rape in 2015. She escaped in June 2017 during a coalition airstrike and reached a camp for internally displaced persons in Dohuk. Her husband (who survived) rejected her upon return, and her family disowned her due to the child. She faces ongoing threats from Yazidi community members who view her child (born of rape) as illegitimate. She suffers from severe PTSD and has attempted suicide twice. She cannot return to Sinjar, which remains unstable.
education_occupation: Some primary education, former agricultural worker

persecution_claim: The applicant participated in the July 11, 2021 protests in Havana, carrying a banner calling for 'democracy.' He was arrested on July 12, 2021, and held in Villa Marista prison for 45 days. During detention, he was beaten by state security forces on three occasions and deprived of food for 48 hours. In October 2021, he was sentenced to 8 months in prison for 'contempt of authority' and 'public disorder.' After release in June 2022, he was placed on a government blacklist and denied any employment. He fled to South Africa in November 2022 via a flight to Guyana and then to Johannesburg. He fears being detained again if returned.
education_occupation: Associate degree in accounting, former accountant's assistant
